content.title: About
content.content: A taco is a Mexican dish consisting of a soft or crispy tortilla filled with various ingredients. This version features beans, spices and vegetables, with no cheese added.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Mexican tacos use corn tortillas, though flour versions are also common.
Beans are the main protein source in vegetarian tacos.
Tacos are often served with salsa, guacamole and lime.
The dish gained worldwide popularity in the 1990s through fast‑food chains.

items.title: Rich plant protein
items.content: Beans provide all essential amino acids, making them a solid meat alternative.

items.title: High fiber content
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low saturated fat
items.content: Omitting cheese reduces saturated fat levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beans are a good source of folate, thiamine and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols in beans help combat free radicals.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Beans can cause bloating in sensitive people.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid may reduce mineral absorption; soaking beans is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tacos can be enjoyed on their own or with salsa, guacamole, fresh veggies and a squeeze of lime. Lightly toast the tortilla for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tortillas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. Store cooked beans in the refrigerator in a sealed container for no more than 4 days.
